title: Affect or effect? A little difference. A big change.
excerpt: A simple way to remember two words that often get mixed up. Learn the difference, then try it in a sentence.
content:
## One letter, two different jobs

Affect is usually a verb. It means to influence or change something.

Effect is usually a noun. It means the result of a change.

## See the difference

- The weather can affect your mood.
- A good night's sleep has a positive effect on your concentration.

## A useful reminder

Think of affect as the action and effect as the end result. This is a helpful rule for everyday English, although both words also have less common uses.

## Your turn

Complete this sentence: Regular practice has a positive ___ on your confidence.

Answer: effect.
author: Gurus Classes of English
